angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 705,440 km at 122.31 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.1756 +/- 0.0197 mas (same row, RUWE 1.14): 122.31 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.014 +/- 0.041 solar radii from Essack et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4465 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170...41E/abstract): 705,440 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.93 +/- 0.06 solar masses from Essack et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4465 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170...41E/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5545 +/- 19 K from Essack et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4465 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170...41E/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Essack et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4465 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170...41E/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4465.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.394, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
